problem.text: The prequantization diagnostic inspected every module and its output state unconditionally. This change adds controls for restricting diagnostic output without restricting the forward pass.

reasoning.text: Keeping loading and forwarding outside the new inspection predicates preserves the state needed by later modules and by final perplexity evaluation. The options select observations, not a partial model execution.

impact.text: Default arguments retain inspection of all modules and states. Weight comparison histograms change even with defaults: their displayed range expands from ±3 to ±4 population standard deviations.

source_notes.text: Read ancestor entry 34d2f1f5fa069b842b8791de8c8db499b3884579, which introduced the diagnostic and its Hessian-free, skipped-global-scale regularization path. It records both a conditional hidden-state histogram stride defect and an unbound verbose-reporting variable.

The task leaves both recorded mechanisms unchanged. inspect_state still slices without requesting contiguity; regularize still reads mse_scale under verbose after its skipped-search branch assigns only g_scale. The diagnostic supplies verbose=False, so its regularization call does not select that latter failing combination.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” discusses decoder parameters and regularize's scaling decisions. Its relationship here is inferred from the same regularize implementation called by inspect_module; it does not establish a motivation for these new CLI options.

Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” and issue #42, “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” report conversion failures. Their relevance is inferred from nonfinite-state diagnostics and tracebacks naming quantize.py, whose regularize function this script uses. Neither report establishes that this options-only change repairs those failures.

limitations: No repository implementation, Torch operation, CUDA kernel, model evaluation or terminal rendering was executed. The Python check models predicates, bin-width arithmetic and flattened indexing only.
The inspected evidence supplies no empirical justification for choosing four rather than three standard deviations.
Whether inspect_state's device conversion materializes a contiguous copy was not executed; the stride observation is conditional on the sliced view retaining its row gaps.

chapters.title: Select diagnostic modules while retaining the complete forward pass

claims.text: The parser adds integer -fl/--from_layer and -tl/--to_layer, both defaulting to None, plus the store_true switch -nim/--no_inspect_modules. The interval includes from_layer and excludes to_layer.

Despite their names, the bounds compare against idx from enumerate(model.modules): they select zero-based top-level module positions, not an explicitly resolved decoder-layer number. No validation rejects negative or reversed bounds; the comparison predicates determine the resulting selection.

Both bounds gate inspect_module before forwarding and inspect_state afterward. no_inspect_modules gates only inspect_module, leaving selected state diagnostics enabled. Thus it skips Linear weight extraction, weight statistics, random-sign preparation and diagnostic regularization, rather than merely suppressing their printed output.

Every module is still loaded, prepared for its device, forwarded and unloaded; tensor-cache cleanup remains unconditional. Final next-token perplexity still uses the resulting final state. The existing skip_tokens option remains local to hidden-state inspection.

inspect_module expands both original-weight and regularized-weight histogram ranges to ±4 times each tensor's own population standard deviation, centered on zero rather than on its mean. Bin counts remain histogram_bins // 2 per chart. The hidden-state histogram's middle range remains ±3 standard deviations, and the absolute regularized-outlier thresholds 4 and 8 are unchanged.

Weight histograms pass exclusive=False. The native kernel clamps out-of-range samples into edge bins, so expanding the range changes bucket assignment rather than admitting previously discarded finite samples. At a fixed bin count, the tradeoff is wider coverage with coarser interior resolution; each chart remains independently normalized to its maximum bin count.

A standard-library transcription selected positions 2 and 3 for bounds [2,4), retained those state selections with module inspection disabled, and selected nothing for reversed bounds [4,2). With the default 160 histogram bins, each weight chart has 80 bins: nominal width grows from 0.075σ to 0.1σ, a factor of 4/3.

The new gates narrow exposure to the inherited hidden-state stride issue but do not repair it: selected inspect_state calls retain the same slicing and native histogram path. Whole-parent-tree search located only main's direct inspect_state call.

findings.description: Selected hidden-state inspections retain the inherited mismatch between sliced tensor strides and contiguous native histogram traversal.
findings.trigger: An inspected state has multiple rows and a positive skip_tokens smaller than the context length, and conversion to the selected device leaves the sliced view's row gaps intact.
findings.expected_behavior: Histogram all and only the selected token suffixes from every row.
findings.actual_behavior: inspect_state does not request contiguity. histogram_kernel reads input_ptr[i] for numel elements without consulting strides, potentially counting skipped tokens from subsequent rows while omitting selected trailing elements.

verification.description: Compared the unchanged slice and raw-pointer kernel with main's newly gated direct call. The defect remains conditional within the selected interval; no_inspect_modules does not disable this call.
verification.limits: Literal search establishes the located direct caller, not external callers or actual device-copy behavior.

verification.description: Modeled a contiguous [2,3,2] array with one skipped token per row. Selected elements sum to 52; contiguous traversal from the slice offset sums to 44.
verification.limits: Python indexing model only; neither Torch slicing nor the CUDA implementation ran.

annotation.summary: Adds half-open module-position bounds and a weight-inspection disable switch while retaining full forwarding and perplexity evaluation. Weight histogram ranges widen to ±4σ; selected state inspections retain an inherited conditional stride mismatch.
